chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about the sun: does it purify the ground? He said: “If a place is filthy from urine or other than that, and the sun shines upon it, then the place dries, then salat (prayer) on that place is permissible. But if the sun shines upon it and the filthy place does not dry and remains moist, then salat (prayer) upon it is not permissible until it dries. And if your foot is moist, or your forehead is moist, or some other moist part of you touches that filthy place, then do not perform salat (prayer) on that filthy place. And if the very disk of the sun reaches it until it dries, then that is not permissible.”

key_terms.الشَّمْسِ: the sun, as a means discussed in relation to drying impurity from the ground
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity depends here on the state of the place
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the ground or earth upon which salat (prayer) may be performed
key_terms.تُطَهِّرُ: purifies; removes ritual impurity in the legal sense under discussion
key_terms.رَطْبًا: moist or wet, indicating ongoing transferability of impurity
key_terms.قَذِرًا: filthy or impure due to najasah
key_terms.يَبِسَ: dried, the condition tied to permissibility in the report

ai.seo_question: Does the sun purify najis ground so that salat (prayer) can be performed on it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the effect of the sun on najis ground and the permissibility of performing salat (prayer) on it. It states that when a filthy place is dried by the sun, salat (prayer) on it is permissible, but not while moisture remains or when moisture from the body would contact the impurity.
